content.comment_body: Hi, I want to connect an analog signal to my [product_name], and I am curious about the maximum cable length that will still allow the unit to work reliably. I checked the data sheet of the sonar sensor I am using, but it doesn't specify this information.

Generally, cable length is not a major concern. Lengths of 100 meters or more typically do not pose issues. More important factors include whether the cable is shielded or unshielded, and its proximity to cables carrying high-frequency signals or high currents. Using a 4-20mA sensor usually results in less interference and lower sensitivity to wiring resistance than a 0-10V sensor.

analysis.insight_summary: A user asks about the maximum cable length for connecting an analog signal to a [product_name] unit. The reply explains that cable length is usually not a limiting factor, but signal reliability depends more on aspects such as cable shielding, sensor type, and whether the cable is near sources of electrical interference.
